prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Columbus Ohio for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t truthfully pick a single “best” attorney — the right lawyer depends on the facts of your case and what you want (quick settlement vs. going to trial, level of communication, etc.). I can, however, help you find a top personal-injury attorney in Columbus and tell you how to choose one.

Quick next steps
- If you want, tell me a few case details (date of accident, injuries, whether liability is disputed, insurance limits) and I’ll help narrow the search and suggest what to ask attorneys.
- Or I can draft a short list of questions to use in free consultations and a message you can send to firms.

What to look for in a Columbus car-accident lawyer
- Substantial car-accident/personal-injury experience (not just occasional cases)
- Trial experience and a record of significant settlements/verdicts
- Experience in Franklin County courts and with local insurers
- Clear contingency-fee terms (typical range in practice is about 33–40% depending on timing; confirm exact terms)
- Good client reviews/references and no disciplinary history
- Clear communication: who will handle the file, how often you’ll get updates

Where to search and verify reputations
- Columbus Bar Association Lawyer Referral Service (free/low-cost initial consult)
- Ohio State Bar public records for discipline history
- Third‑party rankings: Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers, Avvo, Martindale‑Hubbell
- Google/Yelp reviews and past client testimonials
- Ask for examples of similar cases and outcomes

Questions to ask in the free consultation
- How many car-accident cases have you handled? How many went to trial?
- Who will actually work on my case (attorney, associate, paralegal)?
- What’s your typical fee and how are costs handled?
- Can you describe a recent comparable case and result?
- Do you advance medical and litigation costs?
- How long do you expect my case will take?
- Can I speak with a past client or see written testimonials?

Important deadlines and practical points
- Ohio statute of limitations for personal injury: generally 2 years from the injury date (there are exceptions). Don’t wait to talk to an attorney.
- Preserve evidence (photos of scene and injuries, medical records, police report, contact info for witnesses).
- Notify your insurer as required but avoid giving recorded statements beyond basic facts until you consult a lawyer.

If you want, I can:
- Help you compile a shortlist (if you give me permission to look up current firms or provide names you’ve found).
- Draft an email or script for intake calls.
- Review responses from attorneys and help compare offers.

Which would you prefer to do next?
